reasons.specificity: The analysis names every Riley text by title, year and uid, distinguishes the five Weber source keys by edition and section, tracks the 28 checked pair candidates versus 70 unchecked windows, and gives source-specific readings for estates/closure, political capitalism, patrimonialism, science-and-values and standpoint themes. It avoids generic 'Riley uses Weber' claims and instead pins fidelity verdicts to specific passages such as E&S pp. 919, 1028-31, 965-67, MWG I/23 A180, and Gerth/Mills pp. 126-27. Minor deduction: a few texts (2Z7GD9IM, EJJLVCUC, C9LPBLYH, VF5R7DTE) receive only one-sentence substantive comment despite having candidate windows, so their distinct roles are thinly covered.
reasons.anchoring: All eleven settled verdicts (F1-F11) carry paired quotations from both the Riley citing clause and the Weber primary window, with edition notes. F2 is verbatim; F5 is near-verbatim despite a minor OCR difference ('lades' vs 'lacks'). F9 is anchored against MWG I/23 pp.598-99 at marginal A180, correctly not MWG printed p.180. F3's 'stretched' verdict is supported by the contrast between Riley's 'bureaucratic and infrastructural capacities' and Weber's monopoly-of-legitimate-force definition. Seventeen unresolved pairs are honestly labelled rather than given spurious verdicts. Slight deduction: RW0011's wording occurs in the supplied primary source (the 'supplements' sentence appears at Gerth/Mills p.127) but the analysis calls it unverifiable because the index route is search-only, not page-resolved; this is methodologically correct but the reader may feel the actual text is present in the packet.
reasons.non_obviousness: The analysis makes several non-obvious distinctions that a casual reader would miss: (1) the difference between MWG printed p.180 and marginal A180 at pp.598-99 for the estate definition; (2) that 'Faultlines' explicitly signals adaptation while earlier texts do not, so fidelity standards differ across the corpus; (3) that the 2025 Riley-Brenner reply revises the political-capitalism concept in response to critics rather than merely repeating 2020; (4) that RW0074 routes to an editorial introduction rather than Weber's own words, making it unusable; (5) that Weber's estate formulation at A180 expressly denies that class position alone determines estate, which limits readings making market interest the governing explanation; (6) that the Gerth/Mills impression held (1948) differs from Riley's cited impressions (1946, 1958). The scope-assessment boilerplate at the end is machine-generated and repetitive, diluting the otherwise high non-obviousness.
reasons.coherence: Attribution kinds, verdicts and sourcing are consistent across the paired-audit table, the F1-F11 ledger, the source-specific reading sections and the coverage table. The 'unverifiable' label in the table matches the explanation in the prose for RW0002-0003 (edition mismatch), RW0074 (editorial voice), and the composite citations. The 'stretched' verdict for RW0023 is consistently explained in both the table row and the F3 ledger entry. One mild tension: the analysis says RW0050, RW0076 and RW0084 are 'textually plausible or accurate' but receive no positive final pair row, yet the body calls RW0076 'accurate' and RW0084 'accurate'—this creates a slight discrepancy between the positive assessments in the prose and the 'no positive row' classification in the table.
reasons.usefulness: The audit delivers what was requested: a paired table for 11 settled pairs with A-side claim, Weber anchor, attribution kind, verdict and reason; an honest account of 17 unresolved pairs with explicit reasons; counts of 28 checked candidates, 70 unchecked windows and 5 Weber source keys; edition/locus notes throughout; and a bounded practice conclusion. The source-specific reading sections map each Riley text to the engagement themes and label Riley's additions versus what Weber supplies. The read-first route of five steps is actionable. The long scope-assessment boilerplate at the end is largely uninformative (all entries are 'inconclusive / malformed scope JSON fence') and adds bulk without value, but it does not contradict the useful content.
reasons.hallucination_risk: No invented Weber quotations appear. The F2 verbatim check against E&S p.919 is exact. The F5 near-verbatim check notes the OCR artefact ('lades' for 'lacks') rather than asserting perfect identity. The analysis correctly warns that the Gerth/Mills 1948 impression held may differ from the 1946/1958 impressions Riley cites and does not assert edition identity. It correctly flags that RW0074 retrieves only an editorial introduction. It does not claim Weber's text is absent when a window is merely a search candidate. The one slight risk is that the body calls RW0011 'unverifiable at the indexed locus' while the actual sentence ('not absolute contrasts but rather supplements') does appear in the supplied primary window at Gerth/Mills p.127; the analysis notes this but the verdict label could mislead a quick reader into thinking the wording was not found in the packet at all.

score.one_line: A thorough paired audit settling 11 of 28 candidates with accurate anchoring, strong non-obvious distinctions (A180/MWG p.180, edition mismatches, editorial-voice window, explicit adaptation signals), and honest unresolved labelling for the remainder, marred only by minor prose-table tension on three borderline pairs and uninformative boilerplate scope sections.
